standard_prerequisites.name: The notion of a property of morphisms of algebraic spaces being etale-smooth local on the source-and-target, in the three forms recorded in the chapter on descent on spaces
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Invoked inside the counted proof (source lines 7851-7860 and 7876-7879) as cross-chapter pointers to the definition and to two lemmas
standard_prerequisites.use: Allows the property to be moved along the smooth base change and along the etale covering used in the comparison.

standard_prerequisites.name: The description of a DM morphism through the existence of an etale presentation of the fibre product over a smooth presentation of the target
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Invoked at the start of the counted proof (source lines 7798-7800) as a pointer to the author lemma lemma-DM (labelled separately in the same chapter)
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the diagram of the second condition out of the DM hypothesis.

core_obligations: First implication: the DM hypothesis provides a scheme etale and surjectively mapping onto the fibre product of the source with a smooth presentation of the target, which gives a diagram of the first kind, and the surjectivity of the resulting map to the source transfers the property (proof lines 7796-7806)

Comparison diagram: conversely the proof takes an arbitrary diagram of the first kind and builds the commutative diagram comparing the two presentations by the fibre products of the corresponding pairs (proof lines 7809-7834)

Etaleness bookkeeping: the horizontal arrows are smooth as base changes, and the two cartesian squares show that the relevant vertical arrows are etale exactly because of the additional etale condition imposed on the diagrams (proof lines 7835-7850)

Transport along the localness: the property moves to the base change by the smooth localness on the target, then to the composite via the etale localness on the source, and finally to the second map using the third clause of the definition with the etale comparison morphism (proof lines 7851-7880)

The representable cases: for representable morphisms the characterisation statement applies, and for a representable morphism with a property preserved under base change the proof checks the condition for an arbitrary base change by a scheme using the same third clause (proof lines 7882-7915)
proof_roadmap: (1)⇒(2)：由 f 是 DM，取满光滑 V → Y 与满 étale U → V ×_Y X（lemma-DM），即得 (1) 型图，并由 U → X 满得 (2)。

(2)⇒(1)：设 (2) 的图与任一 (1) 型图 U' → V'，作比较图 U ← U ×_X U' → U'、V ← V ×_Y V' → V'。水平箭头由基变换光滑；两个笛卡尔方块给出竖直箭头 étale（正是 (1) 型图多加的 étale 条件）。再由 P 的 étale-smooth local 三条：先沿光滑基变换搬到 t，再沿 étale 的 s 前拉得 (h,h') 有 P，最后用定义第 (3) 条与 étale 的比较映射得 h' 有 P。
可表示情形用 descent on spaces 的刻画引理；fppf 局部情形用 Z ×_Y 的基变换图与同一条定义。
difficulty_reason: The counted statement gives the etale-smooth analogue of the standard localness criterion: for a DM morphism of algebraic stacks a property of morphisms of algebraic spaces which is etale-smooth local on the source-and-target may be checked on a single presentation, with the same variants for representable morphisms (author lemma at source lines 7764-7793, label lemma-etale-smooth-local-source-target). The proof (source lines 7795-7916) uses the DM hypothesis to produce the presentation, then proves the converse through a comparison diagram in which the extra etale condition on the diagrams makes the relevant vertical arrows etale, and transports the property along the smooth localness on the target and the etale localness on the source before applying the third clause of the definition (proof lines 7851-7880); the representable cases are reduced to the characterisation for algebraic spaces and to a base change diagram with a scheme (proof lines 7882-7915). The etale bookkeeping in the comparison diagram is the content. H3.
